label: caiso163 asym path ratings
definition: caiso-163 arm B — TREATMENT, and the CAISO KEEPER. Promotes caiso_asymmetric_path_ratings: CAISO's two INTERNAL north-south paths move from the SYMMETRIC TTC estimate the reduced topology ships to their PUBLISHED WECC Path Rating Catalog DIRECTIONAL ratings — Path 15 (Midway-Los Banos) 3,265 MW N->S / 5,400 S->N and Path 26 (Midway-Vincent) 4,000 N->S / 3,000 S->N. Each shipped ttc_mw was only ONE direction's rating (Path 15's 5,400 is its S->N limit, Path 26's 4,000 its N->S limit), so the reverse directions ran up to 65% too loose. Rule 14 [R-ACCURATE] measured-over-estimate; ZERO free parameters — all four numbers were already committed in CAISO_PATH_DIRECTIONAL_RATINGS before the session opened, nothing swept, no residual consulted, DOF ledger carried verbatim at 11 entries / 9 residual. STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY IS THE CLAIM, AND IT IS MEASURED ON FLOWS, NOT PRICES (the caiso-162 lesson — a never-executed mechanism reads on prices as a clean INERT verdict and would write a false matrix I). Against the same-HEAD control the incumbent configuration moved power past a published WECC rating in 1,141 path-hours across 2023-2025; under this keeper that count is ZERO in every hour of every year, and the paths bind as real paths do (Path 15 N->S 307 / 489 / 411 h; Path 26 N->S 1,656 / 1,987 / 2,213 h). Path 15 becomes a path that binds at all: NP15 separates from ZP26 in 237 / 414 / 284 hours, up from 3 / 0 / 1, and the 2024 NP15==ZP26 byte-identity is broken. GATES: all nine criteria IDENTICAL to the control — zero flips, C3a-2025 unchanged at +12.0%, protective C6/C7/C8 all PASS — and the effect on level is nil (-0.004% / -0.015% / +0.010%). THIS ARM OPENS A ROOT-CAUSE ISSUE RATHER THAN CLOSING ONE, disposed of exactly as the prereg pre-committed before solving: the real Path 15 separates the hubs in ~100% of hours with a mean NP15-over-ZP26 basis of +5.95 / +8.58 / +5.73 $/MWh, against this arm's -0.077 / -0.109 / -0.084, so the published ratings are NOT the binding cause of the model's missing N-S basis and the basis moves marginally FURTHER from the measured sign. Under rule 14 and rule 1 [R-STRUCT] that is a DISCOVERED BUG, not a revert — the symmetric estimate was silently absorbing a defect that lives elsewhere, most plausibly the reduced two-link N-S topology and zonal aggregation. The remaining gap is an OPEN investigation and is NOT claimed as closed; no compensating adder was added to hide it. A/B control: 2026-08-03-caiso163-control-asymoff. Prereg: results/calibration/PRECHECK-caiso163-asymmetric-path-ratings-2026-08-03.md. Evidence: results/calibration/FINDING-caiso163-asymmetric-path-ratings-2026-08-03.md.
market_story: Path 15 and Path 26 are the two wires California's north-south power actually crosses, and WECC rates each of them DIFFERENTLY in each direction — Path 15 carries 5,400 MW north but only 3,265 MW south; Path 26 carries 4,000 MW south but only 3,000 MW north. That asymmetry is why NP15, ZP26 and SP15 are separate prices at all: on a spring afternoon the south's solar surplus wants to travel north and hits the 3,000 MW Path-26 ceiling, and on a summer evening the north's hydro wants to travel south and hits the 3,265 MW Path-15 ceiling. The model shipped one number per path, each of them the LOOSER direction, so the LP could always find a way around the congestion and the three hubs collapsed onto one price — in 2024 NP15 and ZP26 were byte-identical in all 8,760 hours. Installing the published ratings makes the wires behave like wires: 1,141 hours in which the model had been shipping power past a rating WECC does not grant are gone, Path 26 binds south-to-north through the solar belly in roughly a quarter of hours, and Path 15 starts separating the northern hub from the middle one. It does NOT yet reproduce the real basis — CAISO's hubs part company in essentially every hour and by $6-9/MWh, while this model parts them in 3-5% of hours and by cents — and that gap is left standing as an open root-cause question about the reduced two-link topology, not papered over.
